name: Black Sable Services (fictional)
inspired_by: Gulf-financed mercenary forces of the 2015-2026 era: contractors recruited internationally (Latin American, African and Eastern European veterans) under Western or Gulf-registered front companies, paid by Gulf investors and client governments to fight in Yemen, the Horn of Africa and the Sahel, with Emirati-style vehicles and Chinese-built armed drones in support. No real company, state funder, logo or person is depicted.

doctrine.summary: A large, well-paid but mixed-quality force: Latin American ex-soldiers make up the assault companies, Western and Eastern European veterans lead them, and local auxiliaries hold ground. It brings money and hardware that most local forces lack: Nimr armoured vehicles, armoured Land Cruisers, gun trucks and Chinese-built armed drones flown by contractor crews. Leadership is competent; the rank and file are uneven and loyalty follows the pay. It fights hard for ports, airfields and coastal towns and is ruthless in protecting its clients' commercial interests.
doctrine.fireteam: Sections of 8 under a Western or East European team leader; Spanish-speaking pairs; local auxiliaries as extra rifles.
tactics: Mounted assaults in Nimrs with gun-truck support
Armed-drone strikes ahead of assaults (Wing Loong-class, game support asset)
Seizing and holding ports, airfields and coastal roads
Night raids by a small elite team
Bounty-hunter pursuits with fast gun trucks across open desert

body_armor.notes: Ballistic helmets and plate carriers for contractors (medium, ceramic or steel); local auxiliaries light or none.

vehicles.notes: Chinese-built armed drones flown by contractor crews (game support asset).

as_target: Retake a port or coastal town Black Sable seized for a rival client
Recover recruits held in debt bondage or abandoned by the company (rescue)
Gather evidence of abuses for an NGO or UN client
Survive a Black Sable bounty-hunter pursuit during extraction

rivalry.role: nemesis (Captain-confirmed (2026-10-10)): big-budget rival with the most hardware and the least cohesion
bids_on: Port, airfield and coastal-road security in yemen_red_sea and horn_of_africa
Counter-terror contracts paid by Gulf clients
Mine and logistics security in the sahel
rivalry.bidding_behaviour: Overbids on hardware (offers drones and armour) and wins Gulf-funded contracts unless the player's rep with the client is high.
shows_up_as_enemy_when: The player works against Black Sable's client in Yemen or the Horn of Africa
Black Sable holds a counter-contract on the same port or VIP
The player rescues recruits from a Black Sable camp (story beat)
rivalry.bounty_hunter_trigger: When the player damages a Black Sable client's assets, the company posts a bounty and sends fast gun-truck pursuit teams with drone overwatch.
defeat_rewards: Salvage of Western and Gulf kit (CAR 816-pattern rifles, plate carriers) at loot caps
Captured drone ground-control intel (temporary drone-free window in the theatre)
Recruits who defect to the player as hireable squadmates (proposal)
Reputation with Somali and UN clients
rivalry.escalation: Repeated defeats bring Nimr columns and armed-drone overwatch, then a named field commander.

notes: FICTIONAL company; no real company, funder, logo or person is depicted. Inspired by the reported pattern of Gulf-financed mercenary recruitment (Latin American veterans in Yemen and Sudan, 2015-2026). In game it has business ties to Gulf states (positive relations with are and sau), which never fight alongside it openly. Hostile to the player as a rival, never a client or vendor. Its Nimr and Wing Loong use is a game assignment (proposed); its M-ATVs are Captain-confirmed (2026-10-10): the existing voxel models are fielded by the operators listed in their catalogue files. Captain chose it as the player's main nemesis (2026-10-10); the rest of the rivalry object stays a proposal.

rivalry (all fields except role; the nemesis role is Captain-confirmed)
